s.g: To dig a hole by poking; especially, to dig a small hole in soil for the purpose of planting a bulb or seed.
To move in a rapid, cautious manner; especially, with movement like a mouse or rat.
A dibber (gardening tool).
One of the small bones in the knee joints of sheep uniting the bones above and below the joints.

dib.f: (astronomy, spectroscopy) Abbreviation of diffuse interstellar band.

s.g: (chemistry) (of an acid) containing two replaceable hydrogen atoms
(chemistry) (of a salt) having two atoms of a univalent metal
A tool with a handle on one end and a point on the other, used in the garden to poke holes in preparation for planting seeds, bulbs, etc.
One who dibs.
A pointed implement used to make holes in the ground in which to set out plants or to plant seeds.
(transitive) To make holes or plant seeds using, or as if using, a dibble.
(intransitive) To use a dibble; to make holes in the soil.
(intransitive) To dib or dip frequently, as in angling.
(slang, UK, originally Manchester, countable) A police officer, especially one serving with Greater Manchester Police.
(slang, UK, originally Manchester, uncountable) Preceded by the: the police.
s.x: Watch out, lads! Here comes the dibble!

dibbles.f: third-person singular simple present indicative of dibble

dibbs.f: Alternative form of dibs (“the right to use or enjoy something exclusively or before anyone else”).

s.g: (organic chemistry) Two benzo groups in a single molecule
Of or pertaining to two blocks together.
(chemistry, of a polymer) Having two different blocks per macromolecule.
(inorganic chemistry) boron hydride, B₂H₆, a colourless explosive gas with a nasty smell; it has an unusual structure in which two of the hydrogen atoms form a bridge between the two boron atoms
(informal) The right to use or enjoy something exclusively or before anyone else.
s.x: I call dibs on the hammock!

s.g: (informal) Used to claim this right.
(informal) To claim a temporary right to (something); to reserve.
(dated) A sweet preparation or treacle of grape juice, much used in the East.
(obsolete) A child's game, played with dib bones or stones, throwing them up from one's palm and catching them on the back of the hand.
(slang, archaic) Money.
(organic chemistry) Two butyl groups in a molecule
